subject: Should 'besag' and 'bym' models give identical results?

messages.author: 461a0c7d7557dffc
messages.subject: Should 'besag' and 'bym' models give identical results?
parts:
I was playing with the Bym model from Vol. 1 of INLA examples.

I was wondering if 'bym' nad 'besag' models should give exactly the same results.

Using the code below I get very similar, albeit not identical results. Is that behaviour to be expected?

CODE:

library("INLA")

data(Germany)
g = system.file("demodata/germany.graph", package="INLA")
source(system.file("demodata/Bym-map.R", package="INLA"))
summary(Germany)

Germany = cbind(Germany, region.struct=Germany$region)

# besag
formula1 = Y ~ f(region.struct, model="besag", graph=g) +
  f(region, model="iid")

result1  =  inla(formula1, family="poisson", data=Germany, E=E)

# bym
formula1.bym = Y ~ f(region, model = "bym", graph = g)
result1.bym = inla(formula1.bym, family="poisson", data=Germany, E=E)

summary(result1)
summary(result1.bym)

messages.author: 9a89594e7fcb7aad
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Should 'besag' and 'bym' models give identical results?
parts:
Yes, but I think the default priors are different, that's why you get different results.

H
